```{r,echo=FALSE}

while(T){
    part = sample(1:199,1)
    whole = sample(20:199,1)
    perc = part/whole*100
    if(perc%%1==0 && perc<100 && whole != 100 && perc!=50){break}
}

```

Question
========

A store's normal retail price for a trinket is $`r whole`. 

The store is having a sale; and the sale price of the trinket is $`r whole-part`. What is the percent discount?

(Please include `%` in your answer.)


Solution
========

This scenario represents a percent decrease. It is beneficial to find the scale factor.

$$\text{scale factor}~=~\frac{\text{new price}}{\text{old price}}~=~\frac{`r whole-part`}{`r whole`}~=~`r (whole-part)/whole`$$

To find the percent decrease, you can subtract the scale factor from 1. (And represent the answer as a percentage.)

$$1-`r (whole-part)/whole`~=~`r perc`\%$$

The alternative route is to find how many dollars cheaper the sale price is, and then divide this by the retail price.

$$\frac{`r whole`-`r whole-part`}{`r whole`}~=~\frac{`r part`}{`r whole`}~=~`r part/whole`~=~`r perc`\%$$
